title: Chicken Enchiladas with Red Sauce
subtitle: Shredded chicken in corn tortillas, baked under a smoky red chilli sauce
excerpt: Shredded chicken thighs rolled into corn tortillas and baked under a deep red ancho chilli sauce with a layer of melted cheese. Serve with soured cream and fresh coriander.
sourceNotes: Chicken enchiladas with red sauce: a Tex-Mex staple drawing from Mexican enchiladas rojas. The red sauce is based on dried ancho chillies and tinned tomatoes, adapted from classic Mexican-American home-cooking sources. Chicken thigh filling is a US home kitchen adaptation of the traditional shredded chicken ('pollo deshebrado') used in Mexico.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble and freeze before baking for up to 3 months. Bake from frozen, adding 15 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.batchNotes: Make double and freeze one tray unbaked.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead, cover and refrigerate. Bring to room temperature before baking.

content.text: Chicken enchiladas with red sauce are corn tortillas filled with moist shredded chicken and baked under a rich, dark red ancho chilli sauce. The sauce is made from dried ancho chillies and tinned tomatoes, blended smooth and simmered until it thickens to a coating consistency. The whole dish bakes in 25 minutes.

items.prepNote: soaked in boiling water for 20 minutes, then drained

content.text: Ancho chillies are dried poblano peppers with a mild, fruity heat and a deep colour. Soak them in boiling water for 20 minutes to soften, then drain and blend with the other sauce ingredients.

Season the chicken thighs with the cumin, smoked paprika, and salt. Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the thighs for 6-7 minutes on each side until cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes, then shred with two forks.

Drain the soaked ancho chillies and blend with the tinned tomatoes, garlic, and cumin until smooth. Pour into a saucepan with {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock. Simmer over medium heat for 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens to a coating consistency. Season with salt.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Spread a ladleful of red sauce across the base of a roasting dish.
Dip each corn tortilla into the warm red sauce for 10 seconds. Lay flat, spoon shredded chicken down the centre, scatter over some cheese. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the dish.

Pour the remaining red sauce over the rolled enchiladas. Scatter the rest of the cheese on top. Bake at 190°C for 20-25 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and catching at the edges. Rest 5 minutes, then top with soured cream, coriander, and spring onion if using.

items.cause: Ancho chillies over-soaked, or seeds left in
items.fix: Soak for 20 minutes, not longer. Remove the seeds and stems from the soaked chillies before blending; the seeds carry most of the bitterness.

items.cause: Not dipped in sauce, or sauce was cold when dipped
items.fix: The sauce must be warm when you dip the tortillas. Keep it at a low simmer and work one tortilla at a time.

items.cause: Chicken overcooked before shredding, or not mixed with any sauce
items.fix: Pull the chicken at 6-7 minutes; it should be cooked through but still moist. Stir a spoonful of red sauce through the shredded chicken before filling.

items.symptom: Sauce too thick to pour over
items.fix: Add a splash of stock or water and stir. The sauce should be thick enough to coat a spoon but pourable.

content.text: Chicken enchiladas with red sauce are a Tex-Mex staple, descended from Mexican enchiladas rojas. The ancho chilli sauce gives the dish its characteristic deep colour and mild, earthy heat. In the US, baked enchiladas became a fixture of weeknight cooking through the 1970s as dried chillies and tinned tomatoes became widely available. The result is a dish that looks and tastes far more involved than the work it takes to make.
